fact: The Minister of Agriculture and Livestock of the Government of National Unity announced on 7 April 2026 the launch of a platform for complaints, comments and inquiries from farmers and citizens, with follow-up of action taken; no case count is given.

The General Authority for Communications and Informatics announced the Tawasul platform to receive citizens' complaints about telecom services, count and track them with operators and let citizens follow resolution.
The Citizen Service Centre's own page says it received over 4,000 requests and complaints on its first working day, 12 October 2021, taken via Facebook by thirty agents.

The Citizen Service Centre's own page says tickets are verified by an agent and referred to the delegate of the ministry concerned, with first-day requests mostly on Finance and Health and the rest distributed among the other ministries.

The Libya Herald reports that PM Aldabaiba launched the Citizen Service Centre, whose first stage takes citizens' complaints and inquiries by email and delivers them to the competent authority; no case count is given.
The Central Bank of Libya launched the LYPay website with an online platform for submitting complaints and inquiries about the instant payment service; no case count is given.
